text: Costs 5 wood and lasts 120 seconds; limited to 20 people. Does not cover the whole city or batch relocation.
Manually stoke the fire to spend 1 wood, raise the fire level by one, and reset the 5-minute cooldown.
Waiting for the road to be repaired
The valley must first secure enough food for its own people
Pending: tools 1, medicine 0.5, wood 1, food {变量1}
The new tools are enough to open another clinic and school. Expansion will require iron ingots and machine parts, as well as more doctors and teachers.

Lessons ring out from the school, and the convoy brings back the valley's new harvest. This place is starting to look like a small town. As the population grows, people begin discussing who should make the decisions.
At the end of the old highway, someone has raised a plastic shelter against the river wind. Twelve people live beneath it. Several have patches of hardened skin.

The guide says their altered bodies have not taken away their speech or their memories. They clear land and grow food, but lack tools and medicine. They will not entrust their lives to an outsider in charge.
You note what the valley lacks. Send tools and food first, then discuss repairing the road together.
The team notes the coordinates and heads back to the old highway. You can return whenever you have enough supplies.
Tools have reached the valley's farmers, and the food you sent has made up for the shortfall during road repairs.

The valley agrees to exchange goods, but they will continue to manage their homes, fields, and council themselves. Every 60 seconds, the convoy delivers 1 tool and 0.5 medicine in exchange for 12 food; the trip also costs wood and travel rations.
This is only a mutual aid agreement. Closer ties can be discussed once you have built a relationship.
The valley has become the first mutual aid settlement. As long as the road is clear and supplies are ready, the convoy will make its trips on schedule.
The goods have been delivered. The valley will wait until you have time to discuss opening the road to traffic.

Twelve people live in the valley, waiting for tools and help repairing the road.
Maintenance supplies to the supply outpost have run out, so contact is temporarily cut off. Service can resume once food and wood are stocked.
Supplies have reached the outpost again. Pipeline inspections have resumed.
Food is running low. People are working hungry, and have slowed down.
People have food to share again. Work across the settlement is gradually returning to normal.
